text:
The six papers start from the compact complex six-spheres
constructed by Claude and L.~Alp\"oge and from Engel's elliptic-surface
description. In Paper~I, the theta transformation law and the integral
root norms determine the periods and moduli, while the corner meridians
and the Albanese nome obstruct extension at the two ends. In Paper~II,
the torsion term in the differential sequence identifies the missing
step in the cited vanishing argument and gives the exact replacement
criterion. In Paper~III, actual fibre framings and integral attaching
maps determine the homotopy classes and the resulting manifolds.
In Paper~IV, the full cusp charts, the tensor-frame return and the
relative Pontryagin calculation determine the smooth monodromy on
every retained fan; an explicit family gives a generator of $\Theta_7$.
In Paper~V, rank-six lattice data and their period extension give the
complex fourfold on $3\mathbb H\mathbb P^2\#(-\mathbb H\mathbb P^2)$.
In Paper~VI, normalization, local Milnor fibres and compact-stratum
cohomology give the Euler sign for all degenerations in its stated
torus-fibration class. Each numbered result below supplies the precise
scope and the morphisms used in these mechanisms.

For the zero $[\mu]$ of $\wp_\tau$ selected by the cusp
branch, the missing period is
\[
 \beta^{\rm part}=\frac{6i}{\pi}\Log
  \frac{\vartheta_1(\mu,\tau)}{2\sqrt3\,\eta_D(\tau)}.
\]
The two theta transformation identities give the prescribed affine
period laws, and the cusp value fixes the additive constant
(\ref{fam:src:C.1.1}).

The exact domain is $0<|w|<216$. The normalized theta norm
at a zero of $\wp$ has maximum $\sqrt2$, attained precisely over
$t=1$; the real period determinant therefore stays nonzero precisely
on that disc (\ref{fam:src:C.2.3}).

For
$w_1=r_1\varepsilon+k_1d$, $w_2=r_2\varepsilon'+k_2d$,
$3\nmid r_1$, $2\nmid r_2$, and cusp winding $l_0$, the complete
invariants are
\[
 \left(|12l_0-4r_1-3r_2|,\ e^{-\pi i(c+k_2)}\right).
\]
The finite norm equations determine the parity obstruction and the
remaining cusp winding determines the integer $p$
(\ref{fam:src:B.2.1}).

At each fixed nonzero $u=w^2$ there are two sphere
isomorphism classes, exchanged by a positive $u$ circuit. The
order-four norm quotient detects their difference, and the family
with fixed logarithmic data closes over the punctured $w$-disc
(\ref{fam:src:B.2.2}, \ref{fam:src:B.2.3}).

For coprime multiplicities $(3k,4l)$, the fixed-data period
subgroup is $2kl\Z$, giving $2kl$ classes at fixed $u$.
The two norm images are multiplied by $k$ and $l$, so their central
congruences become $k\mid n$ and $2l\mid n$
(\ref{fam:src:B.3.1}, \ref{push:src:E.1.2}).

At every torsion specialization of $P$, the normalized
norm is algebraic and is given exactly by a division-polynomial
value. The distribution identity fixes its multiplicative constant,
so cancellation at $mP=\pm P$ leaves an algebraic expression
(\ref{ari:C.4.2}, \ref{ari:C.4.3}).

The Albanese nomes of the two reduced multiple fibres are
$q_2=iw/216$ and $q_1=-w^2/48^3=(27/64)q_2^2$.
The invariant-coordinate lattice, including its affine half-period,
and the two exact theta values determine these constants
(\ref{ari:C.2.1}).

The conjugate member has parameter $1-\bar c$, so real
structures occur precisely on the imaginary $w$-diameter, in two
holomorphic-conjugacy classes. The explicit reflection and cap
meridians show that every nonempty fixed manifold is $S^3$
(\ref{fam:src:B.4.2}, \ref{mapsI:src:A.3.1},
\ref{mapsI:src:A.3.2}, \ref{mapsI:src:A.3.3}).

The monodromy group has index twelve in the integral
stabilizer of $d$. It is the kernel of the character
$\chi(B,x,t)=t+6(x_1+x_2+x_1x_2)-\alpha(B)\pmod{12}$;
the commutator and its two conjugates generate the required
Heisenberg lattice (\ref{fam:src:F.1.1}).

On the null locus of $\psi(d,Jd)$ there is a dense set
of points with infinite monodromy stabilizer. On either nonzero
locus the stabilizer in the real parabolic is compact, and the
family period map embeds the $t$-line properly in the relevant
quotient (\ref{fam:src:F.2.2}, \ref{fam:src:F.2.3},
\ref{fam:src:F.3.1}).

The N\'eron--Severi lattice of every regular fibre is
the integral kernel of one displayed period equation, and its
intersection square is $-2\operatorname{Pf}(E)$.
The same Hermitian form gives the projective and elliptic-quotient
criteria with the actual fibre orientation
(\ref{fam:src:D.1.4}, \ref{fam:src:D.1.6}).

The Hodge numbers are the following table, with rows
indexed by $q$ from $3$ to $0$ and columns by $p$ from $0$ to $3$:
\[
\begin{pmatrix}0&0&0&1\\0&1&2&1\\1&2&1&0\\1&0&0&0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The cotangent direct images reduce them to line bundles on
$\Pp^1$; the last connecting rank is fixed by the nonzero scalar
$\mu_s(z_2)=4i\sqrt\pi/(3^{3/4}\Gamma(1/4)^2)$
(\ref{inv:A2.2}, \ref{inv:A3.1}).

The Fr\"olicher sequence satisfies
$E_1\ne E_2=E_\infty$, and the positive-degree ideal in the
Bott--Chern algebra has square zero. The Hodge table and the
Betti numbers force the differential ranks; the fibre class
and its explicit primitives determine the products
(\ref{inv:C1.1}, \ref{inv:C2.1}, \ref{inv:C3.3}).

The relative one-forms have torsion exactly along
$S_1\cup S_2$; the cusp module is torsion-free and fails to be
locally free. The explicit modules for $t=s^m$, $t=xy$ and
$t=xyz$ give this correction to the printed torsion description
in Claude--Alp\"oge, Remarks~1.3 and 9.21
(\ref{inv:A4.1}, \ref{inv:A4.2}).

Every tangent twist has an explicit cohomology
formula. Integral twists are root-line bundles on $\Pp(3,4)$;
nonintegral twists reduce to finite Koszul modules at the
resonant fibres and a length-one cusp term
(\ref{inv:D4.1}, \ref{inv:D4.4}, \ref{inv:D4.5}).

For the standard data,
$h^q(T_X)=(1,1,1,0)$, the Kuranishi germ is a smooth
one-dimensional germ, and $\operatorname{Aut}(X)=\C^*$.
These are credited results of DGKX version~1, re-derived
here through the root-curve Koszul complex and the integral
translation sheaf. The same root calculation gives
$(1,1,1,0)$ for every coprime $(3k,4l)$ sphere family
(\ref{fam:st:A.5.2}, \ref{fam:src:B.4.1},
\ref{push:src:E.2.1}).

The untwisted pinching has explicit semistable
and nodal fillings, while its proposed smoothing to the
six-sphere family is excluded by the virtual Euler number.
The plumbing has virtual Euler number zero and a smooth
six-sphere has Euler number two
(\ref{push:src:A.1.2}, \ref{push:src:A.2.2},
\ref{push:src:A.3.2}, \ref{night:P2.10}, \ref{night:P2.11}).

After the cover $w=r^6$ the sphere family fills
over $(\Pp^1\times\Delta_r)\setminus\{(\infty,0)\}$,
with a twelve-cycle over the ordinary central base.
The equations $X_iY_i=r$ compactify the long period,
and the actual finite translations permute the components
freely (\ref{push:src:B.4.19}, \ref{night:P2.3}).

No flat proper filling exists at $w=0$, after any
finite cover, for any admissible twist or any coprime
$(3k,4l)$ family. Commuting meridians propagate one ratio
along a connected corner fibre, while its two ends have
the incompatible values $0$ and $-p$
(\ref{push:src:B.4.33}, \ref{night:P2.7}, \ref{night:P2.9}).

No flat proper extension crosses any point of
$|w|=216$. The intrinsic anticanonical divisor carries
an Albanese curve with invariant $J(iw/216)$, whose
rational-cusp growth makes the whole circle a natural
boundary (\ref{push:src:D.1.3}).

At a boundary parameter the total root quotient
has a Hausdorff central fibre equal to a circle for rational
$a=\Re c+3/2$ and a point for irrational $a$.
All nearby additive-group limits are determined by an
explicit surviving dual lattice; the quadratic term in
the period matrix produces the additional nonseparation
(\ref{push:src:D.2.3}, \ref{push:src:D.3.1}).

At the eleven rational nonspecial CM parameters,
the theta norm is an explicit positive algebraic factor
times $e^{-\widehat h_O(P)}$. The local division identity
computes every finite-place factor on an integral minimal
model, and the product formula supplies the archimedean
term (\ref{ari:C.6.1}, \ref{ari:C.6.3}).

The norm has one coarse critical point, its
maximum at $t=1$, and each lower level is a Jordan
curve strictly star-shaped about $1$. The exact
derivative is negative along every ray because the
normalized critical factor satisfies $|1-X|<1$
(\ref{ari:C.8.15}, \ref{push:src:D.4.8}).

Two questions remain open in the retained
scope: a literal coefficient atlas for the global
Bott--Chern representatives, and transcendence of the
normalized theta norm at the specified non-torsion
arithmetic points. The known global classes and the
exact height identities reduce these questions to
the concrete gaps recorded in the final part
(\ref{inv:C3.8}, \ref{ari:C.7.1}--\ref{ari:C.7.12}).

For a reduced hypersurface $S\subset Y$, torsion in
$\Omega_S^1$ contributes ambient cotangent sections through a
connecting-map kernel.  The two endpoint vanishings on p.~692 of
\cite{CDP2020} leave exactly this kernel; they determine the desired
vanishing only after its injectivity has also been proved
(\ref{cdp:st:A.1.1}).

A nodal cubic times $\PP^1$ has a one-dimensional
ambient cotangent space for every gluing parameter, while both
proposed endpoint spaces vanish for every nontrivial gluing
parameter.  Normalization preserves the conductor-supported
section responsible for the difference (\ref{cdp:st:B1}).

The conclusion of \cite[Proposition~7.3]{CDP2020}
holds through unitary local systems: the transgression character
has zero first cohomology on every fibre support, and a
torsion-free holomorphic one-form injects into that cohomology
(\ref{cdp:st:A.4.7}--\ref{cdp:st:A.4.9}).

For $s$ deleted values on a base of genus $g$, the
number $r$ of irreducible deleted fibre components is
$r=2g+s-1+t'-b_1(Y)$, where $t'$ is the dimension of the
monodromy coinvariants of $H_1(F,\Q)$.  The complement records
those coinvariants in its first homology.  The rational formula
is credited to \cite[Section~10.5, p.~91]{AC2026}; the integral
refinement is \ref{cdp:st:D.1.2}.

Under the integral CDP hypotheses the very general
fibre is a two-torus or a Hopf surface of algebraic dimension
zero.  Adjunction and divisor Riemann--Roch restrict the surface
invariants; the corrected integral component count and the
explicit monodromy comparisons remove the remaining entries
(\ref{cdp:st:C.3.1}).

For a torus fibration with $b_1(Y)=b_2(Y)=0$ whose
reduced supports are irreducible or have normal crossings, each
support has nonnegative Euler number.  Summing these numbers and
using $e(Y)=2-b_3(Y)$ gives $c_3(Y)\in\{0,2\}$; the rational
normalization contributes two and the other irreducible cases
contribute zero (\ref{night:P4.58}).

Under the integral CDP hypotheses, the generic
vanishing $H^q(Y,T_Y\otimes L)=0$ for $q\ne1$ holds exactly
when the Picard pullback to the normalization of every irreducible
nonnormal critical support is nonzero.  A zero pullback preserves
the conductor section for every twist and forces
$H^2(Y,T_Y\otimes L)\ne0$ for every $L$
(\ref{cdp:st:C4f}).

The tangent cohomology of every integral twist of
$X$ follows from three split root-curve direct images and one
length-two root-chart module.  The map to
$H^2(\mathrm dP_6,K)=\C$ has rank one exactly for
$n\in\{-6,-3,-2\}\cup\Z_{\ge0}$; at $n=-1$ its source is
one-dimensional and the map is zero (\ref{cdp:st:C5b}).

Trivial rational monodromy forces $c_3(Y)\le0$ in
the torus-fibred Betti class, because a persistent positive-index
obstruction would resolve into components of geometric genus
zero and force nontrivial nearby monodromy.  A holomorphic
three-piece filling realizes equality with
$H_1(Y,\Z)=H_2(Y,\Z)=0$
(\ref{cdp:st:D.2.5}, \ref{cdp:st:D.2.7}).

Rank two of the torus Kodaira--Spencer tensor at one
regular value makes every small deformation retain the
holomorphic fibration.  The same cup-product map kills each
Artin-order map obstruction, and the relative graph space turns
these lifts into a holomorphic family, including nonreduced bases
(\ref{cdp:st:E6}).

The two-parameter and Liu--Rollenske constructions
have tangent cohomology $(1,2,2,0)$ and smooth two-dimensional
Kuranishi germs.  A positive $m$-comb has
$(2m+1,8m+1,6m+1,0)$ and a smooth germ of dimension $8m+1$:
root-curve cohomology gives the dimensions, and actual period
sections supply all tangent directions
(\ref{cdp:st:E13}--\ref{cdp:st:E15}).

The specified coprime $(3k,4l)$ families retain
their discrete data at the centre of a holomorphic deformation
disc whose punctured members lie in that family.  The intrinsic
pencil, the finite root charts, and the cusp period extend those
data by the exact analytic comparisons in the deformation-chain
theorems of the body.

The Poincar\'e line bundle gives a torsion higher
direct image in the scope of the printed local-freeness claim;
a square-zero embedded point survives every divisor twist; and
positive combs have $2m+1$ global vector fields.  These explicit
objects give the corrections in \ref{cdp:st:E12},
\ref{cdp:st:E17}, and \ref{inv:E2.4}, with their source scopes
retained.

For the fixed attachment data, the family closes
after the parameter is lifted through $u=w^2$.  The odd return
changes the multiple fibre's Albanese curve, so it does not
identify the two $w$-values; the tangent-cohomology calculation
remains the one stated in \ref{cdp:st:E14}
(\ref{ii:LR:covering}).

The tangent cohomology and Kuranishi germ of a
positive comb are determined above.  The individual splitting
of the rank-three kernel $K_m$ still requires the actual
period-section map: the supplied existence family does not
specify the transition matrices of one smoothed $12$-tooth
member (\ref{inv:E2.3}).

The quotient of the regular family extends across the cusp
through the explicit target solid torus constructed in Paper~I.
Agreement outside the cusp alone leaves all twelve elements of
$\pi_6(S^3)$ available: pinching a small interior six-ball adds any
chosen element.  The target and collar conditions of the repaired map
specify the extension used in the subsequent calculations
(\cref{mapsI:src:A.2.1,maps:src:A.2.2}).

The marked quotient has
$[e]=6\nu'=\eta_3\eta_4\eta_5$, the element of order two in
$\pi_6(S^3)=\Z/12$.  A regular inverse image is a three-torus;
the monodromy calculation identifies its normal framing with its Lie
framing, whose real $e$-invariant is $1/2$
(\cref{maps:src:B.1.1,maps:src:B.1.2}).

The holomorphic algebraic reduction $f:X\to\PP^1$ is
null-homotopic.  Its explicit factorization through the circle quotient
contains the normalized power map of degree $3\cdot4=12$ on $S^3$,
which kills $\pi_6(S^3)$ (\cref{maps:src:B.2.1}).

The cusp collapse retaining the angular coordinate represents
$\eta_4\eta_5\ne0$ in $\pi_6(S^4)$.  At a triple point its
regular inverse image is a two-torus, and the explicit normal-frame
comparison makes this the Lie-framed torus of Arf invariant one
(\cref{maps:src:B.3.1,maps:src:B.3.2,maps:src:B.3.3}).

The regular torus mapping cylinders, the finite affine caps
and the marked honeycomb cusp fit into a finite CW model with cell
counts $(5,20,45,56,42,17,3)$.  The integral attaching maps give the
homotopy type of the six-sphere
(\cref{maps:src:B.5.1,maps:src:B.5.2}).

The prescribed degree-$N^2$ relative Kummer cover of the
cusp, for $N>1$, has no extension to a smooth finite cover of the
whole threefold.  Monodromy continues its marked lattice to one
whose primitive ray indices cannot occur in a smooth cover of the
entire periodic fan.  A finite flat normal completion exists and
is described separately (\cref{maps:src:C.1.1,maps:src:C.1.2,maps:src:C.1.3,maps:src:C.1.4,maps:src:C.1.5}).

For the original marked family with fundamental group
$\Z/d$, where $d$ is prime to six, the universal cover has
$H_2=\Z^{d-1}\oplus\Z/d$, $H_3=\Z/d$, and Euler number
$2d$.  Its cusp divisor products and finite-coefficient cubic
evaluations determine the complete Zhubr invariant, hence one
oriented diffeomorphism type $M_d$ for each $d$
(\cref{maps:src:D.1.1,maps:src:D.1.4,maps:src:D.1.6,maps:src:D.1.9,maps:src:D.1.11}).

The natural-line construction has a complete marked sphere
classification on the twenty-one rank-one Mordell--Weil profiles:
$59$ sphere patterns on $50$ initial rows.  Twelve profiles have
unbounded sphere multiplicities, four have only logarithmic order
one, and five have no sphere output.  The integral refinements
identify the minimal simply connected nonspherical outputs and
the weight-$d$ Engel manifolds.  For OS49 the latest free-cap
calculation retains the extra torsion present outside the coprime
sector (\cref{maps:src:D.2.28,maps:src:D.2.44,maps:src:D.2.45,maps:src:D.2.46,maps:src:D.2.47,maps:src:D.2.48,night:P3F.34}).

Moving the zero of the line-bundle linearization gives a
proper analytic family with one ordinary double point.  Its two
smooth sides are the original six-sphere and $S^3\times S^3$;
the latter carries a complex structure with algebraic dimension
one (\cref{maps:src:D.3.1,maps:src:D.3.2,maps:src:D.3.3}).

The transverse fibre product with the specified elliptic
surface, with its explicit small resolution, is a compact complex
fourfold with $K=\Pi^*L^{-5}$, algebraic dimension two, and
signature two.  Its degree-four intersection form is
$\langle1\rangle\oplus\langle1\rangle$; its Hodge data exclude
membership in Fujiki's class $\mathcal C$
(\cref{maps:src:E.1.2,maps:src:E.2.1}).

The reference $(3k,4l)$ family has return zero on its
reference fan for every coprime pair.  Its two characteristic terms
cancel on the actual page, and the physical-line comparison fixes
the sign of the nonzero values in the other families.

For the selected E6 order-three collision with
$M_6=\mathcal O(6G-O)$, quadratic cap and retained finite character,
the fixed-scalar source loop has physical pair $(-27,-12)$ and
class $24$ on every vertical fan. The full common boundary map of
each ruling change gives, on an arbitrary basis fan $P$, the class
\[
 -4+\frac32(S-1)-\frac{27}{8}(S^2-1)\pmod{28},\qquad
 S=x^2+xy+y^2,\quad (x,y)^t=P^{-1}e_2.
\]
Its image consists of sixteen classes.

For the original $M_6$ family with its quadratic norm-one
cap, fixed scalar, retained finite character and original selected
height, a full positive $\epsilon=w^{-1}$ loop has physical pair
$(-4,8)$ and class $27$ on the initial fan. Its complete fan image
consists of the fourteen odd residues modulo $28$.

The selected-infinity calculation extends to both complete
cap progressions: $M_6$ with translation by $-G$ and $m=3l+2$,
$l\geq0$, and $M_2$ with translation by $-3G$ and $m=3l$,
$l\geq1$. Both primitive norm signs, every retained finite character,
the entire annular reference and every selected lattice-basis fan
are included. Each initial physical pair is $(-4,8)$, and each full
fan image consists of the fourteen odd residues.

For the original E6 point line
$M_6=\mathcal O([6G]-[O])$, translation by $-G$, the quadratic
cap $(m,n)=(2,1)$ and its prescribed finite character and full
annular reference, the selected-I3 source loop has physical pair
$(47,-4)$ and class eight on the initial fan. Its complete
lattice-basis fan image is all of $\mathbb Z/28$. Every class has
an actual word of at most seven native flops from the initial fan.

The selected-I3 result extends to every $M_6$ reduced
cap $m=3l+2$, $l\geq0$, both primitive norm signs, every admitted
finite character and the full prescribed annular reference. Each
cap uses its common strict scalar range with the quadratic
reference. Both characteristic integers and every native fan map
are preserved. Each such cap therefore realizes all twenty-eight
classes, with the same explicit witness words.

For $M_2=\mathcal O([2G]-[O])$ and the three
chronological translations by $-G$, every good cap $m=3l$,
$l\geq1$, either primitive norm sign and each admitted finite
character have initial and vertical physical pair $(-3,-12)$.
For each chosen cap and its reference the scalar lies in their
common strict contraction range. Every selected basis fan has
the actual integer
\[
 A(P)=-\frac38(S-1)(S-3),\qquad
 S=x^2+xy+y^2,\quad (x,y)^t=P^{-1}e_2.
\]
Its exact image modulo 28 has sixteen elements.

Every lattice-basis fan in the specified scalar families
has an exact integer calculation of its return.  The calculation
starts from a vertical fan, transports the complete source, line,
unit and cap maps through an Euclidean fan word, and solves the
target-prism equations after each flop.  The scalar polynomial
$KL(S-1)(S-3)/8$ from the earlier plan is false.

In the specified fixed-edge comparison the flop sends the
physical index $A_M$ to $7A_M$ modulo 28.  The OS45 reference family
has class three and hence its positive covers realize every class;
the multiplier and sign follow from the same physical transfer and
the unchanged native free generators.

The completed one-cap, two-cap and selected-cusp families
have the characteristic pairs and all-fan algorithms given below.
Each value is transported through an explicit source, line and
endpoint map; the remaining source-moduli attachments are stated
separately in \cref{night:P3K.75}.

The complete E7 four-boundary groupoid gives a closed
source-infinity formula on every fan.  The E6 source, Cartier and
root maps identify its completed selected-cusp loops with the same
selected-cusp algorithm, and extend its specified unselected and
native-infinity loops over proper discs, giving return zero there.

The displayed rank-six monodromy and the specified affine
fillings produce a three-connected eight-manifold with integral middle
form $3\langle1\rangle\oplus\langle-1\rangle$.  The primitive cusp
collapses five fibre generators, while the actual order-four boundary
map kills each remaining order-two torsion class with coefficient one.

The genus-two pencil
$y^2=x^5+\lambda^3x+\lambda^4$ gives the required rank-three period
planes.  The actual morphism is the projection of
$\ell_0\wedge\mathcal H_{\mathrm{dR}}$, followed by a holomorphic
splitting of the rank-six extension; a scalar shift removes its real
intersection with its conjugate.

The period planes extend over the two finite root charts and
the marked cusp, giving a compact complex fourfold diffeomorphic to
$3\mathbb{HP}^2\#(-\mathbb{HP}^2)$.  Its characteristic vector is
carried explicitly to $(1,1,1,1)$, after which the known smooth
classification and homotopy-sphere absorption identify the oriented
manifold.

The marked family is parametrized exactly by $\mathcal U$:
its members are pairwise nonisomorphic, have algebraic dimension one
and automorphism group $\mathbb C\times\mathbb Z/2$, and admit no
antiholomorphic isomorphism for this fan.  The real-intersection
function determines the parameter domain; the invariant line and
one half-period determine the automorphisms, while the actual
reflected cusp map fails to preserve a ray of the chosen fan.

Every supplied rank-six integral datum with its affine
orders, twists, clutch and marked primitive cusp has a terminating
conjugacy and integral-topology calculation.  A different, explicit
period-domain construction gives holomorphic transverse periods with
any prescribed finite cusp jet on the punctured base; the polarized
abelian-surface source is excluded by its actual two-line filtration
and the Euler-parity equation.

Every reduced fibre support has nonnegative Euler
number.  On a reducible support the normalization and conductor
give an exact sum of nonnegative contributions; on an irreducible
support finite-character duality and the local conductor calculation
give the value zero or two.
Euler additivity and the skew middle pairing therefore give
$B=\PP^1$, $c_3(Y)\in\{0,2\}$, and $b_3(Y)=2-c_3(Y)$
(\ref{cdp:st:C.2.G.1}).

The equality $c_3(Y)=0$ holds exactly when every
support has its zero-Euler normalization and conductor form.
For reducible supports, equality in each nonnegative summand
forces all blowups and conductor singularities to disappear:
the normalizations are smooth minimal Hopf or non-K\"ahler
elliptic surfaces, and the conductor maps are finite
unramified covers of smooth elliptic curves.

The parity of a torus-degeneration support holds
without the global Betti conditions: its Euler number is
even.  All even integers occur after explicit curve and
point blowups of a product torus fibration
(\ref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.1}, \ref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.2}).
